newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures reverse direction as NY surge.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures reverse direction as NY surge.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures reversed an earlier downward trend and motored higher in the afternoon after speculative short-covering in New York lifted sentiment in London.
But prices finished below their ceilings, hammered by profit-taking , traders said.
"London was extremely quiet and prices drifted lower until New York spiked higher," said one.
Benchmark May contract stood $23 firmer at $1,556 a tonne after ranging between $1,498 and $1,575.
Chartwise, support is seen at $1,500. Traders said a move to below $1,450 could trigger heavy long liquidation by commodity funds, the main driving force behind the recent stunning price rally.
Spot March was also $20 higher at $1,555 but below its peak at $1,575. March/May spread narrowed to $1 from Wednesday's $12 finish.
The day's volume reached a modest 5,099 lots, with the rollover of March positions into forward months dominating the activity.
New York's March contract jumped to a fresh contract high of 150.80 cents a lb just after London closed following a buying spree by speculators.
Traders said the London market was otherwise looking to continue its consolidation in a correction to the recent rally.
"What people are looking at is a couple of days consolidation before it takes another leg up," said one.
Technically, the market's outlook remained constructive, analysts said. Resistance is pegged at the recent high at $1,630 a tonne basis March while support was seen at $1,424.
News Colombia's leading independent coffee growers' association declared a moratorium on debt payments came after both London and New York markets were closed.
One London trader said: "It is an internal payments problem between the growers and the banks. I don't think it would affect the outflow of coffee into the market."
